solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A great deal of rubbish in skip

indicators.note: a great deal of something is most but not all of it, so the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: tripe is nonsense, rubbish talk

explanation.surface: Somebody has piled a lot of junk into a builder's skip.
explanation.walkthrough: The skip looks like a waste container, but it is the verb: to skip is to hop lightly, as a TRIP along is. A skip is British for a large open rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip, in the old sense, is to move with light quick steps, which is exactly how one skips along.

clue.text: Crazed assailant punched by hard marine

indicators.note: a punch drives something into its target, so one letter is driven inside the other string
someone crazed has lost their order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A deranged attacker gets thumped by a tough Royal Marine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine' looks like a soldier in the surface, but it is the adjective, and the answer is a rare word from Greek thalassa, the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Thalassian is a learned adjective meaning of or relating to the sea, the same sense as the ordinary word used here.

clue.text: An inspirational helper?

parts.note: surface reading: a mentor or coach who motivates people
setter's reading: inspiration literally means breathing in, so this helper aids drawing air into the lungs

explanation.walkthrough: Inspiration first means breathing in; the question mark warns that the motivating sense is a decoy for the medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An asthma sufferer's handheld device delivers medicine as the user breathes deeply, so it literally assists respiration.

clue.text: Definitively voluble performers perhaps run separate schedules out of line

indicators.note: to be out of something is to be without it, so one letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
separate as an adjective, meaning set apart
schedules are lists of items or times
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Talkative actors run their timetables independently and out of step with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separate' is the adjective, not the verb, and 'out of line' strips the L from the schedules.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians in hip hop deliver fast rhythmic speech, so they are by their very nature highly talkative entertainers; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Maybe naval duty stirred up carnage around House

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it, so one string wraps the other
stirring mixes things thoroughly, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Naval service stirred up bloodshed around the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' reads as service in the surface, but it is a charge levied: anchorage is also the fee paid for mooring in a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the place where vessels moor, anchorage is the toll a ship pays for the right to lie at anchor, a kind of levy.

clue.text: Bill throttles the most acidic little pest

indicators.note: throttling means gripping round the throat, so one piece closes around another

parts.note: AD, short for advertisement, is a bill or poster
pH 1 sits at the acidic extreme of the scale, written as PH plus I for one

explanation.surface: A person called Bill strangles a tiny, extremely sour-tempered bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemistry is the trick: acidity is measured by pH, and the lowest reading, pH 1, is the most acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are tiny sap-sucking insects that gardeners fight constantly, so a small garden nuisance fits.

clue.text: Traitor gave terrorist bombs

indicators.note: a bomb blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A double agent supplied an extremist with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombs' looks like the thing handed over, but it is the verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tergiversator is someone who turns their back on a cause or keeps changing sides, a renegade or apostate.

clue.text: Chief form of wrestling before crowds

indicators.note: to crowd something is to press in all round it, so one piece is hemmed in by the other

parts.note: sumo is Japanese heavyweight wrestling
pre is the prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: The main type of wrestling puts on shows in front of big audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowds' reads as a noun for spectators, but it is the verb for hemming something in.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge of an organisation, the top boss or head.

clue.text: Possibly left Man Utd?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: left is one example of a position or flank
second meaning: a sports team, Manchester United being one

explanation.walkthrough: The slash separates two definitions; the football club tempts a solver toward a political left wing reading. Man Utd is Manchester United, the English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a flank or position such as left or right, and a team fielded in a sports match.

clue.text: Played harmonica without working tongue

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so the letters are moved around freely
without means lacking, so some letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone played the mouth organ without their tongue doing the work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints tonguing on a harmonica, but 'tongue' is a language here.
explanation.definitionFit: Amharic is the official working language of Ethiopia, and tongue is a common literary word for a language.

clue.text: Fresh discussion on denial surrounding old note

indicators.note: surrounding something means enclosing it on all sides, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a negation is a denial
O is the abbreviation for old
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Talks start again after someone denied something involving an old memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as a written memo, but it is a musical note from the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Negotiating a deal a second time means reopening talks, so new bargaining over terms already agreed.

clue.text: Tough stuff that may indicate a problem for setter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally a firm cushion of hardened material
second meaning: a canine ailment, a setter being a breed of gun dog

explanation.walkthrough: The setter is not the crossword compiler but the dog. Hardpad is a thickening of a dog's paw pads, a sign of distemper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes toughened material literally, and names the paw-thickening symptom of a viral disease in dogs.

clue.text: Very tired, pleasure-seeking soon enough

parts.note: all in is an informal phrase for exhausted
good-time describes someone devoted to having fun, as in a good-time girl

explanation.surface: An exhausted reveller will be done with partying before long.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the wordplay into two adjective phrases that sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells an impatient person that something will happen eventually at the proper moment, so shortly rather than now.

clue.text: Opposition point of view supports rent rise

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it follows the other
rent means torn apart, so these letters are ripped up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a stance is a position or attitude on an issue

explanation.surface: An opposing viewpoint backs an increase in what tenants pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent rise' reads as a housing complaint, but 'rent' is the past participle of rend, torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is the act of opposing or refusing to accept something, so a force set against it.

clue.text: Recruit selection from US Pro Golf

indicators.note: a selection is a run picked out of something larger, so the letters are lifted straight from the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A new player is picked from the American professional golf tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprog is British slang, used in the services, for a raw new recruit; it also means a child.
explanation.definitionFit: In British military slang a sprog is a newly enlisted, inexperienced trainee, the lowest newcomer.

clue.text: Before taking vitamin, endlessly gnaws into part of joint

indicators.note: one thing coming before another puts it first in the line
without ends means both the first and last letters are cut away

parts.note: a grievance that rankles gnaws into you
vitamin B1, thiamine, written out as B plus ONE

explanation.surface: A dog chews into the knuckle end of a roast after taking its supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: Vitamin B1 is spelt as a letter and a number word; 'joint' tempts toward a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The talus is the bone forming the lower part of the hinge between leg and foot.

clue.text: Vigil after cat caught bird

indicators.note: one piece coming after another is placed second in the sequence
to catch words is to hear them, so we want what is heard rather than written

parts.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat
a wake is a watch kept over the dead

explanation.surface: A mourners' watch follows the cat's capture of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' is the sound signal, not the cat's hunting: said aloud, the pet name and the watch make the seabird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small cliff-nesting gull of northern oceans, named for its call.

clue.text: Division of land troops occupying everything — too much

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: an army occupying territory sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, excessive
men are soldiers, troops

explanation.surface: An army unit takes over the whole place, which is overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' suggests an army formation, matching 'troops', but it is a plot of land. An allotment is a small rented garden plot for growing vegetables in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a parcel of ground portioned out to someone, originally from a larger area split up.

clue.text: Favours central character in pan-Slav broadcast?

definitions.note: plural noun for a mass noun meaning generous gifts

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard over the air, so the letters come from what is spoken

parts.note: the middle letter of pan-Slav is its capital, an upper-case S

explanation.surface: Someone favours the main figure in a pan-Slavic radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central character' sounds like a hero, but it is the middle letter; in pan-Slav that letter is capitalised, a big S.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generosity shown in handing out gifts or money, the bestowing of bounty on others.

clue.text: Screen pulled back is hiding loo, for the most part

indicators.note: pulling something back takes it the other way, so the letters run from right to left
to hide something is to hold it out of sight inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most but not all of a word drops its final letter

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A folding screen drawn back reveals a lavatory behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: A shoji is a Japanese sliding panel of paper on a wooden frame; loo is British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoji is a translucent partition in Japanese houses, used as a sliding room divider or door.

clue.text: Townie struggles over English socialist disciple

indicators.note: in a down clue, being over something puts it above, so it comes first
something that struggles twists and writhes, so these letters are wrenched out of order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A town dweller wrestles with the teachings of an English leftist follower.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Owen was a Welsh-born factory owner and early socialist whose followers set up cooperative communities.
explanation.definitionFit: Owenites were adherents of Robert Owen, the pioneer of cooperative socialism, so followers of his reformist ideas.

clue.text: Means to regain past job? Cut down unction about head of Personnel

indicators.note: about means close beside, so the pieces stand next to each other

parts.note: to reap a crop is to cut it down

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
unction is anointing oil or salve

explanation.surface: A sacked worker wonders how to get the old post back after the HR head trimmed their perks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' is harvesting, not reducing. The question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: Being named again to a former post is how someone gets back a position once held, so the process is a route back.

clue.text: Write up part of Bible first for primate

indicators.note: writing something up in a down clue runs it upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: An instruction to write up a chapter of scripture before anything else for the archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests a senior bishop to fit the Bible, but it is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The potto is a slow-moving nocturnal African mammal related to lorises, belonging to the order of apes and monkeys.

clue.text: Summit meeting's principle bores expert

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into something, so one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled person

indicators.note: a pun on principal, meaning chief or first, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The central idea of a summit meeting is a bore to a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit meeting' looks like one phrase; it splits into the definition and the start of the wordplay. The spelling 'principle' punningly stands for principal.
explanation.definitionFit: An acme is the highest point of achievement or peak, just as a summit is the top of a mountain.

clue.text: Government security agency almost charges Treasury scientist

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final character is dropped
to charge something is to load or fill it, so one piece is packed inside the other

parts.note: a chest is a store of funds, a treasury
MI5 is Britain's domestic security service

explanation.surface: The spy agency nearly brings charges against a government boffin at the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like accusations, but it is the verb for loading. MI5 is the British domestic intelligence service.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is someone who studies substances and their reactions, one kind of researcher in the physical sciences.

clue.text: Hear a rule detected by auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so what they detect is a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: Listen to a regulation that the accountants turned up in their inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' reads as accountants checking books, but it is used in its root sense of listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call a defendant before a court to answer a charge, which is when a judge hears the case.

clue.text: President that is backing both sides in election held by group of incompetents

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: something held is gripped within another's grasp, so it sits inside

parts.note: a shower is British slang for a useless bunch of people

indicators.note: the two sides of a word are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A president supports both parties in a vote dominated by a bunch of losers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing both sides' looks like political fence-sitting, but backing reverses the abbreviation. Calling a group a shower is a British insult meaning they are hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was the 34th leader of the United States, serving two terms in the White House.

clue.text: Party from England touring Europe's leaders

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so only the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A political party from England tours to meet Europe's heads of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' first reads as a political party to go with 'leaders'; it is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a festive public gathering or celebration, often an outdoor fair raising money for charity.
